title: Saving & Exporting
description: Three different keepers: the browser gallery that autosaves, a NibGlider file of your own, and exports for other programs.

bubble.title: Three different things
bubble.body: The gallery autosaves your work in this browser. A saved file is yours to keep anywhere. An export is a picture or vector file for other programs. They are not interchangeable.

bubble.title: The gallery autosaves
bubble.body: File ▸ Open Gallery shows the gallery: every document kept in this browser. The current one is autosaved as you work, so closing the tab loses nothing — but the gallery lives and dies with this browser.

bubble.title: Save to File keeps it anywhere
bubble.body: File ▸ Save to File… downloads a NibGlider document file — the drawing in NibGlider's own format, layers, pages, and repeat records included. File ▸ Save Gallery instead keeps a named copy inside the browser gallery.

bubble.title: Open File brings it back
bubble.body: File ▸ Open File…, or dropping the file onto the canvas, reopens a saved document exactly as it was. Older gallery-format files still open too.

bubble.title: Export for other programs
bubble.body: File ▸ Export Raster makes pictures (PNG, JPG, WebP); File ▸ Export Vector makes SVG and PDF. Each offers three scopes: the Document Frame, the Current Viewport Frame, or the Selected Objects. An Export Frame shape in the drawing pins an exact export size.
